meta.name: FORGE 77 optional compatibility layer
meta.note: Procedural browser-side equivalents plus pcall-wrapped CET bridges. No third-party mod files are bundled, edited or redistributed. Detection never makes the prototype depend on another mod.

autodrive.note: Cyberpunk 2077 2.3 added vanilla Auto Drive (drive to a tracked map pin, V key). The community 'Auto drive' / 'Auto Drive Enhanced' mods by nobo (Nexus 14680 / 23157) and the 'Auto Drive CET hotkey for Wander' add-on (Nexus 19309) expose related behaviour. FORGE 77 ships its own procedural autopilot for the mech test, and an optional CET bridge that detects these mods via GetMod and hands off a waypoint when they expose a compatible function.
sources: Nexus 19309 — Auto Drive CET hotkey for Wander
autodrive.browserFallback: MF.compat.autodrive.steer() runs a deterministic steering/obstacle-avoidance solver in the procedural pilot test. It works with no mods installed.

crystalCoat.note: CrystalCoat is Cyberpunk 2077's native dynamic vehicle paint (2.2+): a Primary colour, a Secondary colour, a light hue and paint aspects such as metallic / glossy, opened by holding Y while seated. 'Crystal Coat Picker — Hex Codes and Color Library' (Nexus 35571) adds exact hex entry and one-line share codes. Mechs are not vehicles, so FORGE 77 implements a procedural Crystal-Coat-compatible parameter set on its generated mesh and reads/writes the same share-code format; the CET bridge optionally detects the picker mod and reports its status.
crystalCoat.browserFallback: MF.compat.crystalCoat shades every procedurally generated triangle from these fields (Lambert + metallic specular + flake + wear + emissive light bands). No textures, no assets.

pilot.note: Everything in the pilot test is generated at runtime from numbers: the mech mesh comes from MF.shapeParts() + MF.sigGeometry(), the terrain from a seeded value-noise heightfield, hostiles from other roster sig compositions, and the gait from procedural joint rotation. No meshes, rigs, textures or animations are loaded.
pilot.controls: WASD move · mouse look · LMB fire · Shift dash · Space jump jets · Q core burst · E shield · R missiles · V vent · T AUTODRIVE · C camera · P pause · 1–4 companion orders · Y Crystal Coat panel

disclaimer: Compatibility means: the prototype uses the same public concepts, key names and share-code format, and CET optionally detects the other mods with pcall-wrapped GetMod calls. It does NOT ship, patch, require or claim to control those mods, and it does not make a 3D mech driveable inside Cyberpunk 2077. In-game piloting still needs meshes, rigs, animations, VO, the game itself and private base-mod APIs.
